transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-20
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Solutions), Evelyn Hart (CISO, Empire Trustbank), Jorge Alvarez (Head of Infra), Nina Park (Legal), Marco Li (Cloud Eng)

Summary: Private/VPC deep dive focused on network isolation, ingress/egress firewalling, RBAC/SSO patterns, KMS/encryption, audit logs and data residency requirements. Customer is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated banking workloads and needs details on network controls and compliance artifacts.

Topics: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit log integration, KMS/HSM options, data residency EU/US, VPC peering, ingress/egress firewall best practices, egress filtering, bastion/jump hosts, SIEM integration (Splunk/Datadog), certificate rotation.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off, uh, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, and Samir is our SE, Lena's joining for solutions and notes. Could you do a quick roll call from the Empire side?
00:12 Evelyn: Yeah hi, Evelyn Hart here, CISO at Empire Trustbank. Thanks for fitting us in.
00:17 Jorge: Jorge Alvarez, head of infra, thanks.
00:21 Nina: Nina Park, legal.
00:23 Marco: Marco Li, cloud engineering.
00:26 Alex: Great. So agenda — quick compliance artifacts, then dive into VPC/network architecture, ingress/egress, firewalling, KMS and audit logs, and then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
00:34 Evelyn: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in how you isolate tenant data on a private deployment, and how audit logs are stored and delivered out-of-band.
00:43 Samir: Yeah ok, so to start high level — Redwood Private can be deployed in a customer VPC or on-prem package. For VPC mode we do private endpoints and optionally VPC peering or Transit Gateway depending on scale. We support egress control, IP allowlist, and for on-prem we provide an air-gapped installer and offline keying options.
01:05 Jorge: When you say private endpoints — are those ENIs in our VPC or external? How do you handle egress — does traffic leave our network to Redwood control plane?
01:15 Samir: Good q. The control plane can be run in a Redwood-managed plane or in a private control plane inside your cloud tenancy. For the private control plane model, the control plane components sit in your VPC — so no control-plane egress to public. If you use Redwood-managed control plane with Private workers, we use mTLS and an egress proxy but we can lock down egress to only specific IP ranges and use AWS PrivateLink. There was a little earlier typo in doc — we sometimes call it "priviate vpc" in S3 refs, ignore that, sorry.
01:44 Marco: Ok, we need specifics. Our compliance team wants firewall rules, ports, and expected CIDRs.
01:49 Samir: Yep — we'll share a sample firewall table. For the runtime we need outbound to our image registry (if using our hosted images) on 443, optional NTP, and for metrics posting to the observability endpoint if you choose Redwood-hosted metrics. If you want zero outbound to public we support pulling container images from your private registry or using an offline image bundle.
02:12 Evelyn: For audit logs — do you stream logs to our SIEM? Are they stored in your system too? We need separation of duties, and an immutable trail for exfil audit.
02:21 Samir: We support exporting audit logs to your S3 or to Splunk/Datadog via secure forwarders. By default, logs are written to local encrypted storage (AES-256) then pushed to your configured sink; you can opt to disable persistent logs on the Redwood managed side. The log export supports signed delivery and we also provide CloudTrail-style events for control plane operations.
02:42 Nina: From a contractual perspective we need to ensure logs are retained in region and that encryption keys are customer-managed. Do you support CMKs in KMS or HSMs?
02:51 Alex: Yes — we support BYOK via AWS KMS customer-managed keys, and for on-prem we support external HSM integrations and KMS appliances. You can configure envelope encryption so customer CMK never leaves your tenancy.
03:03 Jorge: How's the RBAC model? We need fine-grained roles and SSO (SAML/SCIM) integration.
:03:09 Samir: Redwood's RBAC maps to groups via SCIM from your IdP. You get roles like admin, dev, observer, and model-operator. We also have per-route policy controls and token-scoped permissions. A note — SCIM provisioning can handle group sync but user identifiers sometimes map differently, so there can be, um, a delta you need to reconcile on first sync.
03:35 Marco: Any support for hardware attestation or cert pinning inside our network?
03:38 Samir: We support mTLS for service-to-service and you can do cert rotation via our API or hook into your certificate manager. For stronger guarantees we can integrate with an HSM for signing keys.
03:49 Evelyn: Data residency — we need all inference logs and PII to remain in the EU. Does Private support region restriction?
03:56 Alex: Absolutely — you can deploy the private control plane in an EU region or on-prem in an EU data center. We also have config flags for region-locking so no backups or logs are replicated out of region.
04:08 Jorge: Network isolation specifics — do you use VPC endpoints for model traffic? What's the recommended pattern for ingress?
04:15 Samir: Recommended pattern: place Redwood workers in private subnets with no public IPs, use internal ALBs (or load balancers) fronted by a NAT/egress gateway for necessary outbound. For ingress, we recommend using private NLB + AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering; if you prefer, a reverse proxy or API gateway in your VPC can do JWT validation and forward to worker internal endpoints.
04:40 Marco: What about egress filtering — we need to ensure no unintended egress to public internet.
04:45 Samir: Use route table rules to block 0.0.0.0/0 on the private subnets and only allow specific egress via a managed egress proxy/AWS NAT with proxy ACLs. For image pulls you can use your ECR or an internal cache.
04:59 Nina: Legal: can you provide a template clause for customer-managed KMS and key rotation responsibilities?
05:06 Alex: Yup I'll attach a sample clause — we have legal-friendly language around BYOK and HSM responsibilities.
05:10 Jorge: Ports and protocols — we need a quick list now.
05:15 Samir: Sure, high level: 443 (TLS) for control and data plane endpoints, 2379/2380 if using etcd clustering internally (only internal), 22 only for bastion access (customer-controlled), 123 NTP optional, and ICMP for MTU checks — but we'll send the exact table.
05:35 Evelyn: Are there any default firewall rules Redwood applies? Or do you expect us to manage security groups?
05:42 Samir: By default in VPC mode we recommend customer-controlled security groups; Redwood provides recommended security group templates which you apply. In private control plane we do not change egress rules without your config — it's a push model from your infra team.
06:00 Alex: Quick note on SOC 2 and ISO — we have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation docs; for Private deployments most customers still request the SOC 2 report for our hosted services and the Private deployment checklist plus penetration test summary. We'll share those.
06:14 Nina: Can you clarify separation of duties for ops vs dev? We need role separation and audit hooks to prove who did what.
06:22 Samir: The platform has per-action audit events, including who rotated keys, who rolled models, and who changed policies. Those events are exportable to your SIEM and are tamper-evident — we sign events and maintain an append-only log. There are occasional transcription notes that say "appent only" — sorry, I mean append-only.
06:46 Jorge: How do you handle snapshotting model weights and caching — any chance large artifacts are accidentally copied out?
06:52 Samir: Model artifacts are stored in encrypted object storage. For private deployments you can set bucket policies to ensure objects never leave region and use IAM policies to restrict access. Cache is ephemeral and stored on ephemeral volumes; we can disable auto-backup of cache.
07:10 Marco: For on-prem air-gapped installs, how do upgrades and vulnerability patches work?
07:15 Samir: We provide an offline upgrade bundle and a signed installer. Customers run the bundle through their internal approval process and apply patches; Redwood provides CVE notices and recommended patches.
07:26 Evelyn: Any certification around hardware security modules? We need FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs.
07:32 Alex: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs via PKCS#11 or cloud HSM services. We'll surface vendor names in the docs.
07:40 Nina: Regarding SSO, do you support SCIM for group provisioning and automatic deprovisioning?
07:46 Samir: Yes — SAML SSO for login and SCIM for provisioning/deprovisioning. We also support OIDC for some IdPs. For audit, we log SSO events and provisioning changes.
08:00 Jorge: Network diagrams — can you share an example showing firewall rules and Transit Gateway architecture for multi-region?
08:06 Samir: Yes — we'll attach a diagram. We have a standard multi-region pattern using Transit Gateway + VPC attachments and route tables that restrict cross-region egress. Also, an alternate is Regional private control planes if you need strict physical separation.
08:24 Marco: Do you support VPC Flow Logs export and integration with our SIEM for flow-level telemetry?
08:29 Samir: We recommend enabling VPC Flow Logs to your log bucket and then forwarding to Splunk/Datadog. Redwood doesn't ingest raw flow logs by default; that's typically customer-managed. We can provide guidance on parsing and retention.
08:42 Evelyn: On incident response — what's the process if there's suspected exfiltration?
08:47 Alex: We have an IR runbook we can provide; key points: immediate snapshotting of forensic artifacts, making audit logs immutable, and assisting with containment. For Private deployments your infra team typically controls the initial containment steps; Redwood provides playbook and SE assistance.
09:05 Jorge: Can we do a test where Redwood runs a simulated egress attempt to validate our firewall rules?
09:10 Samir: Yes we do a security validation during onboarding — we can coordinate a controlled egress test and provide a checklist.
09:18 Marco: How do you handle backup encryption keys and key rotation?
09:22 Samir: We support automatic rotation and manual rotation. For BYOK, rotation is customer-managed via KMS; Redwood calls the KMS APIs with your permissions but never persists plaintext keys. For on-prem HSM we can call APIs or you can provide signed tokens for key usage.
09:42 Nina: Are there any data residency gotchas around analytics/telemetry being sent to Redwood for quality monitoring?
09:49 Alex: You can opt out of telemetry or route it to your telemetry sink. For enterprise contracts we include a telemetry opt-out and a data residency clause so no telemetry leaves the specified region.
09:58 Jorge: What about egress to model card repos or weight stores — do you have checks to ensure model downloads are from approved registries?
10:04 Samir: Yes — you can lock allowed registries by policy and enforce image signature verification. If you use our hosted model catalog we can also cache approved model blobs in your private registry.
10:18 Evelyn: How about encryption in transit between workers? Is traffic internally mTLS?
10:22 Samir: Yes — service-to-service is mTLS, keys are rotated and can be integrated with your internal CA if needed.
10:30 Marco: Any bandwidth or MTU considerations for large model transfers?
10:34 Samir: For large transfers use multipart uploads and pre-warmed caches; we recommend jumbo frames on the private network if supported.
10:42 Alex: Quick note — some of our customers use a bastion host for admin SSH and then session jump to nodes; we recommend session recording and ephemeral credentials.
10:52 Nina: On legal — we'll need to add clauses for audit log access and escrow for keys if a termination event happens.
10:59 Alex: We'll provide sample contract language for key escrow and log export on termination.
11:05 Jorge: Ok, on TLS cert rotation — how often do you recommend and can we automate via our ACM or Hashi Vault?
11:12 Samir: We recommend quarterly cert rotation for service certs and automated via your certificate manager — we have integrations with ACM and HashiCorp Vault.
11:20 Marco: For firewall rules sample — can you include examples for NLB, ALB and internal worker security groups?
11:26 Samir: Absolutely, the sample will show SGs for internal-only traffic, bastion SGs, NLB listener rules, and route table examples to block 0.0.0.0/0.
11:36 Evelyn: One more: encryption at rest — do you support per-customer key partitioning so one customer's key can't decrypt another tenant's data?
11:44 Samir: Yes, keys are per-customer in BYOK model; for hosted we use tenant-scoped keys and envelope encryption. For Private you'll manage CMKs per deployment.
11:52 Alex: Any other questions?
11:55 Jorge: I think we've covered most, will review the artifacts.
11:58 Nina: We'll need the legal language and the SOC report.
12:01 Alex: Great — recap and next steps: we'll send SOC 2/ISO docs, firewall rule table, SAML/SCIM sample config, VPC diagram, and schedule a follow-up on-prem network breakout.
12:12 Evelyn: Thanks all.
12:14 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up.
